question: Which 2027 free agents carry positive surplus value — projected dollars of wins vs expected market cost — and does the committed contact-per-WAR discount surface as an arbitrage?
method: For every free agent with both Steamer WAR and a Spotrac market AAV: value_usd = steamer_war * market_usd_per_war, where market_usd_per_war is the MEDIAN of the class's own implied rate (spotrac_market_aav / steamer_war). surplus_usd = value_usd - cost_aav. This mirrors the Marlins' front-office surplus-value framework. The market $/WAR and costs are all from committed data; no rates invented.
caveat: Surplus value is a VALUATION, not a settled mispricing. It answers 'at the market's own median dollars-per-win, is this player priced below that?' It does NOT prove the market is wrong on any one player — a cheap player may be cheap because of injury, age, or role risk. Use it to arrange the shopping list by arbitrage, then weigh the bummers manually. The Hakes–Sauer mispricing test stayed INCONCLUSIVE, so this is the framework the operator decides on, not a theorem.

contact_skill_arbitrage.contact_arbitrage_text: Top-quartile CONTACT hitters cost ~$8.0M per WAR vs ~$15.0M for the bottom quartile (~54% of the cost) — committed Hakes–Sauer run, data/hakes_sauer_results.json. Buying contact/OBP skill is buying wins at roughly half the dollars-per-win of a power lottery ticket. Descriptive contrast, not a proven price effect (the Hakes–Sauer test was INCONCLUSIVE on mispricing); the surplus value below uses one market-implied $/WAR for ALL players, so skill differences show as the market sees them.
